text: The Patriots' offensive woes have reached a crisis point heading into Sunday's 1 PM ET matchup against the Bills at Highmark Stadium, with New England ranking dead last in the NFL at 9.7 points per game—a reality that became impossible to ignore after Jacksonville's Trevor Lawrence threw three touchdown passes in a devastating 35-6 blowout where Drake Maye turned the ball over three times (two interceptions and a fumble) and called his own performance and the offense's showing "unacceptable." Adding insult to injury, the Patriots placed guard Greg Van Roten on injured reserve Tuesday with a thigh injury, further weakening the infrastructure around their young quarterback at a moment when the offensive line can least afford to lose bodies. With beat writers examining everything from whether Maye is being deployed incorrectly to what exactly has unraveled so quickly in the passing game, the quarterback himself appears ready to demand more from within, though the question now is whether personnel changes and schematic adjustments can arrive fast enough to salvage what's become an embarrassing offensive start.
